QF.id: IFSCA Introduction to AML CFT and PF_13

question.text: Which of the following best describes the 'layering' stage in the money laundering process?

answer.text: It involves moving funds through multiple transactions or accounts to obscure the original source of the money
It is the initial step where illegally obtained cash is first deposited into the financial system
It is the final step where laundered money is used to purchase legitimate assets
It refers to physically transporting bulk cash across international borders

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 12-13 of the NISM IFSCA-01 AML and CFT in the IFSC workbook (December 2025) describe layering as the stage where the launderer moves money through financial transactions or accounts to make the original source of the funds difficult to trace. The Trap: Option B describes placement (the first stage, where illegal cash enters the financial system), option C describes integration (the final stage, where laundered funds re-enter the legitimate economy as assets), and option D describes cash smuggling or physical transportation, which is not layering. Note: Trap wording corrected so that placement is correctly mapped to option B (not option A).
